title: Status similarity and syndicate inclusion
x: Status similarity: lower bank status divided by higher bank status
y: Lead bank selects potential bank for stock-offering syndicate
timeHorizon: Formation of the syndicate for one stock offering
setting: A lead investment bank considers including a potential partner in a stock-offering syndicate. Status is market prestige reflected in tombstone positioning, not network centrality. Resource complementarity and prior joint experience remain comparable across the status-similarity contrast.
task: Rate how greater status similarity changes the likelihood of syndicate inclusion. Compare lower X (Lower min/max status ratio) with higher X (Higher min/max status ratio). Use the same X contrast in both contexts. A positive rating means higher X is associated with more Y; a negative rating means less Y. Rate the relationship, not the overall level of Y. Do not interpret this judgment as a measured empirical coefficient.
sharedFacts: The outcome is inclusion in the particular offering syndicate.
Greater status similarity means a higher ratio of the lower to higher status; it is not defined as higher absolute partner status.

sourceEvidence.citation: Chung, S. (A.), Singh, H., and Lee, K. (2000). Complementarity, Status Similarity and Social Capital as Drivers of Alliance Formation. Strategic Management Journal, 21(1), 1-22.
sourceEvidence.measurementNotes: US investment banking syndication; same offering type and resource and tie-history conditions
sourceEvidence.translationNotes: Status is asymmetric tombstone-bracket prestige, not alliance centrality. Changing one bank score also changes absolute status; two zero scores are coded similarity one.
